rationale: The closest clinical add-on comparison for ground black pepper gave inconclusive pain results. Clinical mixtures and topical studies leave the cracked-pepper exposure unresolved. Isolated piperine changed some evoked pain responses in rodents, with lower-dose and assay-specific variation. No clinical cracked-pepper Parkinson pain estimate was identified.

Cold-pressed walnut oil changed climbing in rotenone-exposed flies and cell viability in a separate culture experiment. A cold-pressed oil mouse trial reports lower demyelination scores based on weakness and paralysis. None measured clinical dystonia after oil consumption.

Parkinson diet menus include baked capsicum without a published apathy-item comparison. One dietary trial reports apathy scale changes with conflicting post-treatment comparisons and no identifiable roasted pepper exposure. Another trial gives baseline apathy without a published arm response. Isolated capsiate gave no identified willingness-to-invest-effort change. No direction for clinical apathy after roasted bell pepper is established.
